entities.name: Agapito Colonna
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Agapito Colonna (b. 1325, Rome – d. October 11, 1380, Rome) was a distinguished Italian cardinal, diplomat, and administrator whose ecclesiastical career unfolded during the tumultuous Avignon Papacy and the nascent stages of the Western Schism. As a scion of the powerful Colonna family, one of Rome's most influential noble houses, his ascent within the Church was significantly bolstered by his lineage, which provided him both political leverage and a network of alliances in the complex interplay between the Roman aristocracy, the Papacy, and various European monarchs. He navigated these intricate power dynamics, playing a crucial role in the Church's attempts to restore stability and centralize its authority, particularly in Rome.

Elevated to the cardinalate in 1378 by Pope Urban VI, a decision that intensified the burgeoning Western Schism, Colonna had previously served with distinction as Bishop of Lisbon (1371-1378) and as a papal nuncio to various European courts, including those of Castile and Aragon. His diplomatic missions were critical in securing allegiances and mediating disputes, particularly during the critical period leading up to the Schism. He played a direct role in the efforts to bring papal authority back to Rome from Avignon, demonstrating a keen understanding of both ecclesiastical law and political pragmatism in his service to the papacy.
